'''Harry Horace Harman''' (June 5, 1913&nbsp;– June 8, 1976) was a Polish-born American [[statistician]] known for his work on [[factor analysis]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1976/06/10/archives/harry-h-harman-statistician-dies-pioneer-in-the-technique-of-factor.html|title=Harry H. Harman, Statistician, Dies|date=1976-06-10|work=The New York Times|access-date=2020-02-10|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> A fellow of the [[American Psychological Association]], he served as president of the [[Psychometric Society]] from 1968 to 1969 and of the [[Society of Multivariate Experimental Psychology]] from 1974 to 1975.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Messick |first=Samuel |date=March 1977 |title=Harry Horace Harman (1913–1976) |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02293744 |journal=Psychometrika |language=en |volume=42 |issue=1 |pages=4–6 |doi=10.1007/BF02293744 |s2cid=123019003 |issn=0033-3123|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He died of a heart attack in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], on June 8, 1976.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jackson |first=Douglas N. |date=October 1976 |title=Harry H. Harman (1913-1376) |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1207/s15327906mbr1104_1 |journal=Multivariate Behavioral Research |language=en |volume=11 |issue=4 |pages=378–379 |doi=10.1207/s15327906mbr1104_1 |pmid=26804111 |issn=0027-3171|url-access=subscription }}</ref>{{-}}
